propositions: _lifecycle_index uses dict.setdefault when mapping canonical schema keys to lifecycle notes, causing only the first-encountered note to survive when multiple deprecation aliases or tombstones target the same canonical key, silently dropping the rest
multi-alias collisions on a single canonical replacement key are not yet present in the current registry but pose a latent robustness gap that must be defended against
_lifecycle_index must be rewritten to accumulate all lifecycle notes per canonical key into a list, then join them into a single Lifecycle table cell rendering
single-note lifecycle entries must render byte-identically to the current output to prevent unnecessary regeneration of committed docs/config-reference.md
generated test guards must seed collisions by monkeypatching _cfg_deprecations and _cfg_tombstones onto a real schema key and assert both notes survive in the rendered table row
all existing tests and gates (lint, typecheck, complexity baseline, committed-tree oracle --check) must pass with no regeneration of generated documentation
